## 1. The house of the spider  (`#the-house-of-the-spider`)

Cited ayat: 29:41

> **29:41** مَثَلُ ٱلَّذِينَ ٱتَّخَذُوا۟ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ أَوْلِيَآءَ كَمَثَلِ ٱلْعَنكَبُوتِ ٱتَّخَذَتْ بَيْتًا وَإِنَّ أَوْهَنَ ٱلْبُيُوتِ لَبَيْتُ ٱلْعَنكَبُوتِ لَوْ كَانُوا۟ يَعْلَمُونَ

### Claims

**c1** (29:41): The ayah says that the similitude of those who take protectors besides God is like that of the spider, which took a house.

**c2** (29:41): The ayah says that the frailest of houses is the house of the spider, if they knew.

### One-minute summary

The ayah likens those who take protectors besides God to the spider, which took a house [c1]. It adds that the frailest of houses is the house of the spider, if they knew [c2].

### Complete story

The ayah says that the similitude of those who take protectors besides God is like that of the spider, which took a house [c1]. It adds that the frailest of houses is the house of the spider, if they knew [c2].

### Deep study

The ayah names what is likened (those who take protectors besides God) and what it is likened to (the spider and its house) [c1]. It then states the point of the picture in one clause: the frailest of houses is the house of the spider [c2].

### Kids mode

The ayah says that those who take protectors besides God are like the spider, which took a house [c1]. The frailest of houses is the house of the spider [c2].

### Life lessons (educational interpretation)

Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the picture compares reliance on protectors besides God with a house that is frail [c1][c2]. Another reading is that the ayah closes with the words if they knew [c2].

### What the sources do not establish

- Not established: who the protectors are; the ayah says only protectors besides God and names none.
- Not established: what the house is made of or how the spider built it; the ayah says house and does not describe it.
- The ayah itself uses the word for a similitude (mathal).
- The Arabic awhan al-buyut is rendered 'the frailest of houses'; a scholar may prefer another wording.
